name: ANB Capital
legal_name: ANB Capital Company (a Saudi Closed Joint Stock Company, Single Person Company); formerly Arab National Investment Company
founded: 2007 registration (CR 1010239908 dated 7 Nov 2007; CMA resolution 2007-36-4 dated 5 Jul 2007; CMA licence 07072-37). Commercial operations began 12 Jan 2008 when it took over ANB's investment services and asset management activities. Renamed from Arab National Investment Company to ANB Capital Company on 29 Jun 2022 (same CR).
ownership_summary: Wholly owned by Arab National Bank (100,000,000 shares of SAR 10; 100% at 31 Dec 2024 and 31 Dec 2025). Share capital SAR 1,000m, fully paid (raised from SAR 400m to SAR 1,000m in March 2017). The annual report calls it the bank's 'sole investment arm'. No dividends were declared or paid in 2024 or 2025.
government_link: Indirect at most. The parent, Arab National Bank, is 40% owned by Arab Bank PLC (Jordan), with no government holder above 5% disclosed (see sa-anb). Nothing government-owned at anb capital level.
group_structure: 100% subsidiary of Arab National Bank (sa-anb), fully consolidated by the parent. No subsidiaries other than special purpose vehicles that hold fund assets under CMA rules; these SPVs are not consolidated (AR 2025). Holds a 23.76% associate stake in the Sara Second Real Estate Investment Fund (SAR 325m invested 21 May 2020, equity accounted). Double counting: the parent reports anb capital as its 'Investment and brokerage services' segment (see sa-anb, where the segment total is within SAR 0.2m of anb capital's own SAR 556.2m operating income). Never add this record's figures to sa-anb. Roughly a third of anb capital's own FY2025 operating income came from the parent (SAR 175.9m of SAR 556.2m, calculated from note 17: deposit commission 150.4m, advisory fee 10.0m, discretionary portfolio fees 10.3m, corporate finance 4.3m, custody 0.9m).
footprint: Saudi Arabia only. Head office King Faisal Road, Murabbaa, Riyadh. Four investment centres on the website (checked 12 Oct 2026): Riyadh (2), Al-Khobar, Jeddah. International brokerage reaches GCC, Egypt and US markets through the anb capital Global platform. Also distributes funds through the anb mobile app (parent).
customer_segments: Individual investors (retail, HNW; wealth management for 'individuals, families, entrepreneurs and corporations'); discretionary mandates for corporate, institutional and HNW clients with investable assets of SAR 20m or more; institutional clients served by a dedicated sales team (asset managers, sovereign wealth funds, family offices); corporates and government entities for investment banking; anb retail and affluent clients via the parent.
business_lines: FY2025 operating income SAR 556.2m (audited): asset management fees 181.1m; special commission on cash deposits 150.4m (all placed with the parent); margin lending income 96.0m; investment banking and advisory fees 74.8m; brokerage fees net of Tadawul fees 36.4m; investment gains and other 17.4m. Activities: public mutual funds (14 listed on the website), discretionary portfolio management, 24 closed-ended real estate funds, 4 private equity and venture funds, private fixed income funds, wealth management and advisory, Saudi and international brokerage with Shariah and conventional margin lending, investment banking (ECM, DCM, M&A, debt advisory), sell-side research (since late 2024), and a licence for custody that is not a core activity.

capabilities.wealth_summary: anb capital is the parent bank's sole investment arm and the product engine behind its affluent and private offers (see sa-anb). It reported SAR 24.6bn AUM on a net asset value basis (SAR 28.0bn gross) at 31 Dec 2025. FY2025 operating income was SAR 556.2m, of which asset management fees were SAR 181.1m, margin lending SAR 96.0m, investment banking SAR 74.8m and net brokerage only SAR 36.4m (-22%); SAR 150.4m was interest on deposits placed with the parent. The shelf is 14 public mutual funds (12 Shariah-compliant; Saudi equity, money market, multi-asset and a sovereign sukuk fund), 24 closed-ended real estate funds, 4 private equity and venture funds, private fixed income funds and discretionary mandates from SAR 20m. The Wealth Management page describes research-led advisory and customised portfolios, but publishes no minimums, products or named team beyond the head of the unit. Clients trade Saudi equities in a new app (2025) that has scheduled recurring orders and margin, and international markets (GCC, Egypt, US with fractional shares from USD 1) on the 'anb capital Global' platform, which the site says is powered by Global Trading Network (GTN). 2026 priorities in the annual report: diversify products, grow discretionary mandates, execute a private credit strategy, build joint ventures and partnerships, introduce REITs.

private_banking.detail: anb capital has no private banking unit of its own. Wealth Management (advisory and portfolio management) and discretionary mandates from SAR 20m are the closest services. The parent bank runs Private Banking and the anb Elite proposition (see sa-anb).

asset_management.detail: AUM SAR 24.6bn NAV / SAR 28.0bn gross at 31 Dec 2025. 14 public mutual funds on the website (8 equity, 2 money market, 3 multi-asset, 1 sovereign sukuk fund; 12 Shariah, 2 conventional; SAR and USD money market funds). 24 closed-ended real estate funds, 4 private equity and venture funds (anb Seed Fund, healthcare fund), 2 private fixed income funds and 2 public multi-asset funds launched in 2025. Asset management fees SAR 181.1m in FY2025 (+43%). No fund-level AUM published on the website.

brokerage.detail: Saudi Exchange plus GCC (Qatar, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Muscat, Bahrain), Egypt and US exchanges (NYSE, Nasdaq, OTC; options data). Channels: broker-assisted Central Trading Unit, IVR self-trading, web, apps and a TWS active-trader program. Brokerage value traded SAR 68bn in 2025; brokerage fees SAR 36.4m net of Tadawul fees; Shariah and conventional margin lending (SAR 96.0m income). Institutional sales and trading desk with two new global broker relationships in 2025 (brokers not named). Sell-side research since late 2024.

digital_investing.detail: New anb capital trading app and web platform (2025): conditional and stop-loss orders, digital IPO subscriptions, online margin, scheduled recurring investment orders, watchlists (Shariah, newly listed, growth, ESG), analyst ratings, one-tap switch to the global platform. 'anb capital Global' (e-brokerage for GCC, Egypt, US; web, iOS, Android) is stated to be powered by GTN; fractional US shares from USD 1; open to anb capital clients with a local portfolio and an active anb current account. Funds can also be subscribed in the anb mobile app (parent). Launch date of the new app not stated on the page.

advisory.detail: Wealth Management page: research-based investment advisory and customised portfolios, including Shariah-compliant strategies, 'experienced advisors' (not named). Head of Wealth Management since 2022. Investment banking advisory (ECM, DCM, M&A, debt advisory) is a separate division.

discretionary.detail: Discretionary Portfolio Management for clients with investable assets of SAR 20m and above; process covers objectives, risk tolerance, execution, periodic review and rebalancing. The parent also places a discretionary portfolio with anb capital (SAR 10.3m fee income in FY2025). 2026 priority: 'Grow DPMs'. DPM AUM not disclosed.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or model-portfolio product found on the anb capital website or in AR 2025. The new app offers scheduled recurring orders (automated investing) and three Shariah multi-asset funds (conservative, balanced, growth) act as risk-profiled options.

funds_platform.detail: Own funds only on the website and in the anb app. No third-party fund shelf or fund-platform provider found.

structured_products.detail: No structured products on the anb capital website or in AR 2025. The parent bank's Treasury sells structured deposits (see sa-anb).

private_markets.detail: 24 closed-ended real estate funds (7 launched in 2025; Narjis View Fund exited at 2.3x cash-on-cash and over 50% IRR); 4 private equity and venture funds including the anb Seed Fund (10 fintech investments) and a healthcare fund (Baraya Extended Care); real estate debt structuring; 2026 priorities include a private credit strategy and expanding VC and PE. Two real estate funds bought land in Al Khobar for over SAR 800m on 30 Jul 2026.

islamic_wealth.detail: 12 of the 14 public funds are labelled Shariah-compliant (Shariah equity, SAR and USD Trade money market, multi-asset and sovereign sukuk funds); Shariah margin lending; Business Gate Fund is Shariah-compliant; annual Shariah Committee report (Arabic) published. The firm offers both Shariah and conventional services.
